Docket 1.3.118

**Docket is free to try: run a full audit of any site without a key and see your score, how many problems each area has, and the most important problem in full with its fix. [Buy it once](https://kerr-affiliate-hub.kerrco.workers.dev/buy/docket?src=release-notes), $349, or 4 payments of $87.25, to see all the others, the ranked fix plan and the markup to paste. 30-day refund, no conditions.**

- *Docket no longer says a robots.txt block stops a fetch that a user started.* Its crawler list said blocking
  ChatGPT-User, Perplexity-User or Meta-ExternalFetcher stops that assistant fetching your page when someone asks
  about it. Each operator says otherwise: OpenAI says robots.txt rules may not apply to requests a user starts,
  Perplexity says its user fetcher generally ignores them, and Meta says its fetcher may bypass them. The list now
  says what the operators say, and the crawler data bundled with the app is the current published feed. Claude-User
  still reads as blocked by robots.txt, because Anthropic says it is.
- *Meta AI's search crawler is now checked.* Meta-WebIndexer builds the index Meta AI searches, and Meta says
  allowing it helps Meta AI cite and link to your pages. A robots.txt that blocked it was reported as clean. It is
  now checked beside the ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity search crawlers: blocked by a catch-all rule, it is reported
  at critical severity; blocked by name, it is recorded as your choice. Meta's and OpenAI's ad-review crawlers are
  still not checked, because blocking them costs nothing in search or in AI answers.
- *A competitor blocking Google-Extended is no longer called absent from AI answers.* The competitor comparison
  treated that as its strongest opening. Google-Extended controls Gemini training, and Google's AI Overviews and AI
  Mode follow the ordinary Googlebot rules, so that competitor can still appear there. The comparison now uses the
  same list of search crawlers as the audit.

99 checks across 13 areas.
